answer: Each bonded identity contributes to a shared evidence graph: when k identities coordinate equivocation, detected cross-signatures expose k(k−1)/2 pairs, so the base penalty grows as O(k²), not linearly per account. A further detection multiplier, exp(λk) for λ>0, makes total capital loss rise exponentially with swarm size; escrowed collateral and asymmetric depreciation prevent splitting stake across cedar, basalt, or forge identities from reducing the cost.
